title: NVIDIA releases a foundation model for predictions on tables
friendlyTitle: NVIDIA’s new model makes predictions from ordinary tables
summary: NVIDIA introduced Kumo Tabular, an open foundation model that predicts labels for new rows from a table of examples without task-specific training, tuning or feature engineering. The model comes in three sizes from 28 million to 215 million parameters, supports classification and regression, and is released with code and commercial-use terms.
friendlySummary: Kumo Tabular can look at labelled rows and predict values for new rows without being trained again for each job. NVIDIA provides several model sizes, code and weights.
whyItMatters: Many business predictions concern ordinary tables rather than text, and reducing per-task model development could make forecasting and classification more accessible. Teams should still compare it with strong tree-based baselines on their own data and review licensing, bias and failure costs before deployment.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This may make common business prediction tasks quicker to try. Always compare it with simpler methods and test it on your own data before relying on it.
